race.name: Granfondo Matildica
race.tagline: A 153 km UCI Gran Fondo World Series qualifier over five named Apennine climbs, starting and finishing in central Reggio Emilia.

vitals.start_format: Age-group grids open at 6:30am; competitive Granfondo and Mediofondo riders start together at 7:30am from Corso Garibaldi, followed immediately by noncompetitive riders
vitals.registration: Online registration closes at noon on September 11; organizer rules also permit on-site entry September 12 and from 6:00-7:00am on race morning
vitals.entry_fee: €60 online July 1-September 11 at noon; €65 on site September 12-13; non-licensed riders also need the €20 FCI day license
vitals.feed_zones: Organizer promises refreshments across both routes and at the finish; exact 2026 feed locations are published with the route materials rather than enumerated in the rules
vitals.cutoff_time: Finish on Corso Garibaldi within 6 hours 30 minutes of the official start; riders arriving after 2:00pm are not classified

route_options.name: Gran fondo
route_options.categories: UCI qualifier for women and men 19-49; Italian Granfondo Championship route for eligible FCI categories

route_options.name: Medio fondo
route_options.categories: UCI qualifier for women and men 50+

climate.description: Mid-September in Reggio Emilia can still be warm, while the long route reaches higher Apennine roads where temperatures and rain exposure can change during the day.
challenges: Warm lower roads around Reggio Emilia
Cooler or wetter conditions on the higher Apennine sectors
Six-and-a-half-hour maximum time leaves little room for prolonged stops

terrain.surface: Fully paved roads from Reggio Emilia into the Reggiano Apennines and back; roads are temporarily closed to traffic until the end-of-race vehicle passes

fondo_rating.scoring_notes: Migrated from gravel-race-automation. Original score: 77. adventure dimension dropped, road_surface added. Score recalculated: 74.

course_description.character: A 153 km paved loop that leaves Reggio Emilia for the Reggiano Apennines and accumulates 2,150 m across five named climbing sectors. Vetto, Gottano, and Ramiseto arrive between km 45 and 64; Maillo and Stella add two more four-kilometre sectors after km 95. The 126 km Mediofondo shares the event but carries a separate 1,450 m total.
course_description.signature_challenge: Absorbing the early Vetto-Gottano-Ramiseto cluster without spending the legs needed for Maillo, Stella, and the return to Reggio Emilia.
suffering_zones: Three climbing sectors between km 45 and 64: Vetto, Gottano, and Ramiseto
Stella from km 110 to 114 before the return to Reggio Emilia

logistics.lodging_strategy: Plentiful in historic Reggio Emilia with piazzas, cultural sites, and food/wine.
logistics.transport: Start/finish at Corso Garibaldi, Reggio Emilia. Organized by A.S.D. Cooperatori (granfondo@cooperatori.it, +39 333 6918411). Full services including bike parking, mechanical/medical aid, refreshments, massages, abandonment recovery.

history.origin_story: First held in 1973, Granfondo Matildica reaches its 54th edition in 2026 and is one of the world's oldest gran fondos. It hosted the UEC Gran Fondo European Championships in 2022 and returns to the UCI Gran Fondo World Series as the first qualifier for the 2027 world championships.
notable_moments: UEC Gran Fondo European Championships host in 2022
54th edition combines UCI World Series qualification with the 2026 Italian Granfondo Championship

biased_opinion.summary: A long-running Italian gran fondo with real competitive stakes: 153 km, 2,150 m, five named Apennine climbing sectors, UCI age-group qualification, and the Italian Granfondo Championship on the same long route.
strengths: Five named climbing sectors spread across a 153 km paved course
UCI qualification for 19-49 riders on the Granfondo and 50+ riders on the Mediofondo
Central Reggio Emilia start and finish with mechanical, medical, recovery, and post-race services
weaknesses: The 6.5-hour classification limit demands disciplined pacing and short aid stops
Temporary road closure ends behind the race vehicle, after which riders continue under normal road rules
International riders need the correct racing license or medical documentation
biased_opinion.bottom_line: Choose Matildica for a historic, fully competitive Italian gran fondo where the decisive problem is managing five Apennine sectors across 153 km rather than surviving one headline summit.

final_verdict.one_liner: A 153 km race of cumulative Apennine climbing, where three early sectors set up Maillo and Stella after km 95.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Yes if you want a historic Italian age-group race with UCI qualification, full competitive timing, and 2,150 m of climbing distributed across the day. Skip it if the 6.5-hour classification limit or Italian license and medical-document rules do not fit your travel plan.
final_verdict.alternatives: For a shorter qualifier at the same event, riders age 50+ use the official 126 km / 1,450 m Mediofondo.

eligibility.notes: The organizer's current regulations confirm Sunday September 13, 2026; the 7:30am Corso Garibaldi start; 153 km / 2,150 m Granfondo; 126 km / 1,450 m Mediofondo; 6.5-hour classification limit; current fees; temporary road closure; and top-25% UCI qualification. The organizer's climb page defines five current sectors at km 45-47, 52-56, 61-64, 95-99, and 110-114.
